name: ILAC (MA)

rules.name: Overview
rules.desc:
The purpose of the MA program in Iberian and Latin American Cultures is for students to develop further the knowledge and skills acquired as undergraduates and to prepare students for a professional career or doctoral studies. This is achieved through completing graduate courses in the student’s major area of interest and related areas. Students in this program may not apply concurrently for entrance to the PhD program.
The coterminal degree program allows undergraduates to study for a master’s degree in Iberian and Latin American Cultures while completing their bachelor’s degree(s) in ILAC or a different department. The course requirements for the coterminal MA are the same as those for the terminal MA, and students should be aware that university policy prevents one course from counting for both the BA and MA degrees.

rules.name: Core Program Requirements

children.name: A 200-level or above course in literary or cultural theory
Two 200-level or above courses in Latin American or Latinx/Chicanx literature and culture
Two 200-level or above courses in Iberian literature and culture
One 300-level course in Latin American or Latinx/Chicanx literature and culture
One 300-level course in Iberian literature and culture
36 of the 45 units taken at Stanford
Program Proposal for a Master's Degree (terminal MA, first quarter)
Enrollment in at least two department graduate seminars each quarter
Intermediate-high proficiency in Portuguese or Catalan (OPI)

rules.desc:
Students must complete a minimum of 45 graduate-level units, 36 of which must be taken at Stanford. Students enrolled in the terminal MA program must file a Program Proposal for a Master’s Degree during their first quarter of enrollment. Any changes to the proposal should be reviewed and approved by the Director.
The requirements for the terminal MA and coterminal MA are:

• A 200-level or above course in literary or cultural theory

• Two 200-level or above courses in Latin American (including Brazilian) or Latinx/Chicanx literature and culture

• Two 200-level or above courses in Iberian literature and culture

• One 300-level course in Latin American (including Brazilian) or Latinx/Chicanx literature and culture

• One 300-level course in Iberian literature and culture

• Enrollment in at least two graduate seminars (200- or 300-level) offered in the department each quarter

• Intermediate-high proficiency in Portuguese or Catalan (equivalent to one year of university study; to be assessed by OPI).
Independent study courses (ILAC299 Individual Work, ILAC399 Individual Work) and cross-listed courses originating outside the department cannot fulfill requirements except by consent of the Director.

grading:
MA students in the department must take required courses for a letter grade if available, and they are expected to earn a grade of B+ or better in each course taken. Any grade of B or below is considered to be less than satisfactory. Grades of B or below are reviewed by faculty, and the following actions may be taken:

• The grade stands, and the student’s academic performance is monitored to ensure that satisfactory progress is being made

• The student may be required to retake the course
The principal conditions for continued registration of a graduate student are the timely and satisfactory completion of the university, department, and program requirements for the degree and fulfillment of minimum progress requirements. Failure to meet these requirements results in corrective measures, including a written warning, and/or the possible dismissal from the program.
transferPolicy: Students must complete all units toward a degree at Stanford.
reviewNotes: The audit checks the 45 graduate-level units (courses numbered 200 or above) and the course requirements as ILAC courses at the right level, taken for a letter grade where one is offered: one 200-level or above theory course, two 200-level or above and one 300-level course in Latin American or Latinx/Chicanx literature, and the same in Iberian literature (ILAC 299 and 399 count only with the Director's consent). Faculty expect a B+ or better and review lower grades. Checked by hand: which area each course covers, units taken at Stanford, the program proposal, two department graduate seminars each quarter and the Portuguese or Catalan OPI.
